title: IQM Verifies Full-Chip Entanglement Across 54-Qubit Emerald Superconducting Processor - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IQM Quantum Computers demonstrated GHZ-state entanglement across all 54 transmon qubits of its cloud-accessible Emerald processor, reaching 0.516 fidelity with readout error mitigation, just above the 0.500 threshold for genuine multipartite entanglement. The thin margin shows how hard it is to scale deep circuits on unencoded physical QPUs.

themes.theme: Full-chip GHZ entanglement on IQM Emerald

insights.claim: IQM demonstrated simultaneous GHZ-state entanglement across all 54 transmon qubits of its cloud-accessible Emerald processor, where users previously worked within roughly 30-qubit active partitions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Commercial cloud users may now be able to run circuits across the whole 54-qubit lattice, not just a partition of it.
insights.quote: The achievement validates full-lattice coherence on commercial hardware where users previously operated within ~30-qubit active partitions.
insights.locator: IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX) has demonstrated

insights.claim: On IQM Emerald, a 40-qubit GHZ state reached 0.515 fidelity without mitigation. The full 54-qubit state reached 0.516 with readout error mitigation, just above the 0.500 threshold for genuine multipartite entanglement.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The benchmark clears the bar, but only barely, and the full-chip result relies on readout error mitigation.

insights.claim: IQM prepared the state with an automated scheduling compiler that trades off individual CZ gate fidelities against cumulative qubit idling time. Together with dynamical decoupling, this cut overall processor error rates by up to 50%.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Smarter compilation can give large error reductions on existing hardware without new chips.

themes.theme: Scaling limits of unencoded physical QPUs

insights.claim: The narrow fidelity margin above 0.500 shows how steep the scaling challenge is for deep circuits on unencoded physical QPUs. Keeping the full chip coherent will need faster gates and continuous calibration to stop localized cross-talk from degrading results.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Full-chip entanglement does not yet mean useful deep circuits, so error correction and calibration remain the bottleneck.
